notes: We now choose a representation together with interpretations of the construction operations. This supplies both the concrete representation and its operations, rather than replacing an abstract type name as text. The original code view deliberately shows model lines4–8 only; the signature was already shown on P22.

The register interfaces and comparison map to the corresponding target primitives. Follow the matching source colours: get is red, set is green and ltu is blue. get and set are interfaces of the same register, not two independent registers.

The variables that described connections in the model become the corresponding connections here. In the Idris2 interpretation, they have the matching program representation. Yellow distinguishes the connection emphasis from the primitive boxes. This mapping concerns embedded SynQ operations; arbitrary host-language variables and constructs do not automatically become circuits.

This trace illustrates the resulting input/output behaviour: the detector indicates rises between successive samples. The plotted input and output use different axes. Do not infer physical units or clock rates beyond the source. It is reused execution evidence, not a new simulation and not the formal proof. Transition: For the property stated earlier, we can go beyond an example trace and provide a proof. That next proof does not by itself verify every compiler, synthesis step or target timing property.
